answer: One defense is stake-backed reputation judged over a long horizon: before an agent may enter the harbor of shared services, it posts a sable bond, a deposit that grows with the value it handles, and earns standing only through verified completed work over time. A Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity and risk losing each bond when fraud is detected, so the cost scales with the number of fakes, while an honest agent pays once and keeps its reputation.
